Complaint Handling & Escalation Process
Standard workflow for logging, resolving, and escalating customer complaints.
Document ID KB-CS-003 Version v1.4
Owner Customer Experience Team Last Updated 22 Sep 2026
1. Complaint Intake
(cid:127) Customer raises an issue with the order ID and a description of the problem, through any support channel.
(cid:127) The agent logs the complaint in the case management system with a category tag (delivery, payment,
product quality, seller conduct, other).
(cid:127) An acknowledgement with a case reference number is sent to the customer immediately.
2. Resolution Workflow
(cid:127) Step 1: First-line agent reviews order history, delivery status, and any prior related tickets.

2. Resolution Workflow
(cid:127) Step 1: First-line agent reviews order history, delivery status, and any prior related tickets.
(cid:127) Step 2: Agent proposes a resolution (refund, replacement, compensation, information) within the
documented SLA for that complaint category.
(cid:127) Step 3: If the customer disputes the proposed resolution, the case is escalated to a Senior Support
Specialist for review.
(cid:127) Step 4: Cases involving potential fraud, safety, or repeated seller violations are routed to Trust & Safety.

4. Closing a Complaint
A complaint is only marked resolved once the customer has confirmed the outcome, or after 3 documented
attempts to reach the customer for confirmation have failed. All resolved cases are retained in the system for
12 months for audit and training purposes.
Note: Agents should never close a complaint as “resolved” without either explicit customer confirmation
or a documented final action (refund issued, replacement dispatched, etc.) attached to the case.

daraz Knowledge Base — Internal Policy Document
Delivery Process Guidelines
How an order moves from confirmation to doorstep, including delivery attempt rules.
Document ID KB-DEL-003 Version v1.9
Owner Logistics Operations Last Updated 19 Sep 2026
1. Order Lifecycle Stages
(cid:127) Order Confirmed — payment or COD order successfully placed.
(cid:127) Packed — seller or fulfilment centre prepares the item for handover.
(cid:127) Shipped — item handed to the courier partner and assigned a tracking number.
(cid:127) Out for Delivery — item is with the local rider/courier for final delivery.
(cid:127) Delivered — order marked complete upon customer receipt confirmation.
2. Delivery Attempt Rules

(cid:127) Delivered — order marked complete upon customer receipt confirmation.
2. Delivery Attempt Rules
Each delivery attempt includes a call or SMS notification to the customer ahead of arrival. If the customer is
unreachable or unavailable, up to two further attempts are made on subsequent days before the parcel is
returned to the nearest sorting hub.
3. Express Delivery
(cid:127) Available for select in-stock products in serviceable metro areas.
(cid:127) Delivery completed within 24–48 hours of order confirmation for an additional fee shown at checkout.
(cid:127) Express orders are prioritised at every stage of the fulfilment pipeline.
4. Failed Delivery Handling
(cid:127) After 3 failed attempts, the order is returned to the hub and the customer is notified via SMS/email with

4. Failed Delivery Handling
(cid:127) After 3 failed attempts, the order is returned to the hub and the customer is notified via SMS/email with
rescheduling options.
(cid:127) If no response is received within 5 business days, the order is auto-cancelled and any prepaid amount is
refunded per the Refund Policy.
Note: Customers can reschedule a delivery attempt or update the delivery address (within the same city)
directly from the order tracking page before the final attempt.

(cid:127) Accounts with 3 or more refused COD deliveries within 60 days may be restricted to prepaid payment

daraz Knowledge Base — Internal Policy Document
Payments — Frequently Asked Questions
Common customer questions about payments, answered for quick agent reference.
Document ID KB-PAY-003 Version v1.6
Owner Payments & Fintech Team Last Updated 20 Sep 2026
1. Payment Deduction & Order Status
Q: My payment was deducted but the order shows as failed. What happens now?
A: This is usually a temporary authorisation hold rather than a completed charge. If the order did not confirm,
the hold is automatically reversed by the bank within 5–7 business days without any action needed from the
customer.
2. Changing Payment Method
Q: Can I change my payment method after placing an order?
A: No. The payment method cannot be changed once an order is placed. The order must be cancelled and

A: No. The payment method cannot be changed once an order is placed. The order must be cancelled and
re-placed with the desired payment method.
3. Card Safety
Q: Is it safe to save my card details on the platform?
A: Yes. Saved cards are tokenised through a PCI-DSS compliant payment gateway; the platform does not
store raw card numbers or CVV on its own servers.
4. Duplicate Charges
Q: I was charged twice for the same order. What should I do?
A: Duplicate charges are typically a display issue on the bank's end rather than an actual double charge. The
customer should raise a ticket with both transaction references; the Payments team will verify with the gateway
and refund any confirmed duplicate within 5–10 business days.
5. Installment Plans

and refund any confirmed duplicate within 5–10 business days.
5. Installment Plans
Q: Why don't I see installment options at checkout?
A: Installment plans are only shown for eligible cards from partner banks and orders meeting the minimum
value threshold; eligibility is checked automatically.
Agent tip: Always ask for the transaction reference number and last 4 digits of the card/account before
escalating any payment discrepancy to the Payments team.

daraz Knowledge Base — Internal Policy Document
Refunds — Frequently Asked Questions
Common customer questions about refunds, answered for quick agent reference.
Document ID KB-REF-003 Version v1.5
Owner Customer Experience Team Last Updated 21 Sep 2026
1. Refund Trigger
Q: When does my refund get issued?
A: Refunds are issued after a returned item is received and inspected and confirmed to meet return eligibility,
immediately for orders cancelled before dispatch, and automatically for confirmed failed deliveries where
payment was already made.
2. Refund Destination
Q: Can I choose where my refund is sent?
A: Online payments (card, wallet, bank transfer) are always refunded to the original payment source.

Q: Can I choose where my refund is sent?
A: Online payments (card, wallet, bank transfer) are always refunded to the original payment source.
Cash-on-Delivery orders are refunded to Daraz Wallet by default, with a bank transfer option available on
request.
3. Partial Order Refunds
Q: I only returned one item from a multi-item order — how is the refund calculated?
A: Only the price of the returned item(s) is refunded. Delivery charges are refunded proportionally only if the
entire order is returned.
4. Refund Not Received
Q: It has been longer than the stated window and I haven't received my refund. What do I do?
A: First check the reference number with your bank. If the bank has no record after the maximum stated

A: First check the reference number with your bank. If the bank has no record after the maximum stated
window, raise a ticket with Customer Support including the reference number for investigation by the
Payments team.
Note: Refund FAQs should be read alongside the Refund Policy Overview and Refund Processing
Timelines documents for full context on eligibility and exact timeframes.

Returns — Frequently Asked Questions
Common customer questions about returns, answered for quick agent reference.
Document ID KB-RET-003 Version v1.3
Owner Customer Experience Team Last Updated 21 Sep 2026
1. Return Window
Q: How many days do I have to return an item?
A: Most items can be returned within 7–14 days of delivery depending on category; the exact window for a
given product is always shown on the product detail page and in the Return Eligibility Policy.
2. Proof of Purchase
Q: Do I need the original invoice to return an item?
A: The order ID is required for every return; it is used to look up the order automatically, so a printed invoice is
not strictly required unless requested for a specific case.
3. Change of Mind

not strictly required unless requested for a specific case.
3. Change of Mind
Q: Can I return an item just because I changed my mind?
A: Yes, for most categories, as long as the item is unused, in original packaging with tags attached, and within
the applicable return window. Delivery charges are non-refundable for change-of-mind returns.
4. Damaged or Wrong Item
Q: I received a damaged or wrong item — does the normal return window still apply?
A: No. These cases should be reported within 48 hours of delivery with photo/video evidence, and are handled
outside the standard category return window.
